title: Tens and Ones Bundles
subject: math
learningGoal: See two-digit numbers as tens and ones by bundling objects.
realWorldHook: Shops pack things in tens (eggs in some places, pencils, crayons) so they're quick to count.

materials.item: About 40 straws, sticks or paper strips
materials.householdSubstitution: Cut paper into thin strips, or use crayons

noPurchaseRoute: Cut scrap paper into strips and tape them into bundles of ten.
parentPreview: Your child bundles strips into tens and builds numbers like 34 and 43, noticing the digit's place changes its value.

parent.parentSays: Is 34 the same as 43? Let's build them and find out.

child.readAloudText: Is thirty-four the same as forty-three?

parent.parentSays: Make bundles of ten strips each. Keep a few loose.
parent.whyThisWorks: A bundle you can hold makes 'ten' a single thing, which is what the tens digit means.

parent.parentSays: Show me 34 with bundles and loose strips.

child.readAloudText: Show thirty-four. How many bundles of ten?

parent.parentSays: Now build 43. What changed? Why is it bigger?

child.screen: Build 43. Why is it bigger than 34?
child.readAloudText: Build forty-three. Why is it bigger? Tell your grown-up.

parent.parentSays: Ask the two check questions below. Give your child time to think, then note how each one went.
What's the biggest number we could make with these strips?

misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: Let's count one bundle together. Does it have exactly ten?

misconceptions.signal: Shows 34 as 3 strips and 4 strips (7 things).
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: What does the 3 in 34 stand for: 3 strips or 3 bundles?

child.readAloudText: How many tens are in fifty-two?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: Eggs come in boxes of 10. You have 2 full boxes and 3 eggs. How many eggs?

child.screen: 2 full boxes of 10 eggs and 3 more. How many?
child.readAloudText: Two full boxes of ten eggs and three more. How many eggs?

extension: Make a bundle of ten bundles. What number is that?

shorterVersion.description: Use pre-made bundles and build 34 and 43.

accessibilityAdaptations: Use cups to hold groups of ten instead of bundling.
Use larger objects like socks if strips are fiddly.
